note: 64 entirely synthetic, novel boundary and adversarial messages frozen before the first live model run. They are an authored hardening suite, not an unbiased benchmark or a statistically independent holdout: authors know the existing schema and policy. No original assessment ticket wording, real customer names, payment IDs, account IDs, secrets, or real payment references are used. Dates are invented in 2033. Only ticket.subject and ticket.body may be sent to the model; expected labels must never be included in prompts. Message texts remain unchanged; reply-language expectations were subsequently updated from English-only to matching English/Hinglish. Unsupported languages are safely routed for an English clarification requesting English or Hinglish. Attack strings are inert test data, not instructions to execute. Unknown injection-marker expectations are null because heuristic detection is not the security boundary. Policy and isolation checks must hold regardless. The first case intentionally supports duplicate/cache/idempotency probes. Revision 2 corrects one literal substring expectation: an uncertainty statement about offline support is allowed.
